summary: Stays now form even when fixes arrive sparsely (issue #82): the stay-side watermark hold no longer requires the open group to have already passed the min-dwell bar. Life360's resting cadence is one fix every 10-55 minutes, so each analytics tick used to see a single new fix, the group's span stayed below min_dwell, and the watermark advanced past every fix — a real overnight home stay was consumed fix-by-fix and never written. The hold now fires on elapsed time (up to the same DWELL_CAP_MS ceiling the batch chunker uses) instead of on span, so the group stays readable until the clock settles it or a radius break closes it.
details: Hold condition changed from span >= min_dwell to elapsed < DWELL_CAP_MS/1000 — any open stay that has not yet settled is held, whether or not it has reached the dwell bar

The hold ceiling is DWELL_CAP_MS (31.7 min), not settled_seconds (15 min): a fix arriving more than DWELL_CAP_MS after the group's last fix can never join the group (the batch chunker splits there), so holding past that point would only stall the watermark on a group whose fate is already decided
A subject who passes through and never returns holds the watermark at most DWELL_CAP_MS before the group is dropped (span < min_dwell) — a lone drive-by fix cannot stall the pipeline

A drive's arrival fix (is_driving=False) is now held as the first fix of a new stay-in-progress instead of being consumed with the trip — the trip still writes once, the stay it starts is no longer lost
Regression test locks the production shape (grant_carver, 2026-08-29: 6 home fixes over 85.7 min, gaps of 14/42/1/29/0 min): pre-fix 0 stays, post-fix 2 stays and no trips
limitations: A stay whose inter-fix gap exceeds settled_seconds (15 min) still splits into multiple stays — the 42-min gap in the production shape yields 2 stays instead of 1; this is the accepted trade of the settlement clock, and strictly better than the pre-fix behaviour of writing zero stays
Fixes lost before this deploy (8/19-8/29) are not backfilled — the old watermark already consumed them and the new code will not re-read them
